identity.title: First ALMA Light Curve Constrains Refreshed Reverse Shocks and Jet Magnetization in GRB 161219B

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present detailed multi-wavelength observations of GRB 161219B at $z=0.1475$, spanning the radio to X-ray regimes, and the first ALMA light curve of a GRB afterglow.

evidence.quote: Spectroscopic observations 36 hr after the burst with the X-shooter instrument on the ESO VLT 8.2 m telescope provided a redshift of $z = 0.1475$
The X-ray afterglow was localized to RA = 06h 06m 51.37s, Dec = -26$^\circ$ 47$'$ 29.7$''$ (J2000)

question.value: What do multi-wavelength (radio to X-ray) observations, including the first ALMA light curve, reveal about the forward and reverse shocks, energetics, circumburst density and jet magnetization of GRB 161219B?

evidence.quote: Comparing the RS and FS emission, we show that the ejecta are only weakly magnetized, with relative magnetization, $\ensuremath{R_{\rm B}}\approx1$, compared to the FS.

the 3.6 m Telescopio Nazionale Galileo (TNG), LT, and Keck observations presented by (cite: apm+17) in our modeling.

evidence.quote: We include the contribution of the supernova using a template constructed from the extinction-corrected spectra of SN 1998bw
We imaged the pipeline products using the Common Astronomy Software Application

evidence.quote: All observations utilized J0522-3627 as bandpass and flux density calibrator, and J0614-2536 as phase calibrator.

what.value: Synchrotron spectra from Granot & Sari with weighting schemes of Laskar 2014

evidence.quote: smoothly connected power-law synchrotron spectra described by (cite: gs02) modified using the weighting schemes presented in (cite: lbt+14)

unstated_but_needed: ALMA imaging parameters (tclean weighting, cell, masking) and how flux densities were measured
ALMA flux calibrator flux scale uncertainty
Full multi-frequency data tables (only samples printed)
Exact MCMC burn-in length and convergence criteria (deferred to earlier papers)

analysis_steps.goal: Fit X-ray and UV/optical light curves with broken power laws

method.value: smoothly broken power laws with smoothness fixed y=5

evidence.quote: We fix the smoothness parameters here and in equation [\[eq:bpl\]](#eq:bpl) at $y_1=y_2=y=5$

analysis_steps.goal: Model forward shock with SN and host in all bands

method.value: Synchrotron FS model with jet break, SN 1998bw template, SMC extinction, MCMC

evidence.quote: we carry out a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using the Python-based code EMCEE
We initialized 128 Markov chains with parameters clustered around their best fit values (with a 3% dispersion).

assumptions.value: ISM environment; uniform priors, log-uniform for scale parameters

evidence.quote: Priors for all scale parameters ($\epsilon_{\rm e}$, $\epsilon_{\rm B}$, $n_{0}$, $E_{\rm K,iso}$, $t_{\rm jet}$, and $\Upsilon_{\rm SN}$) are uniform in logarithmic space
We assume uninformative, uniform priors on all free parameters.

analysis_steps.goal: Model reverse shock from energy injection and compare to FS

method.value: Analytic RS scaling relations anchored to cm and ALMA bands; compare with FS scaled by Lorentz factor

evidence.quote: We present a comparison between the observed RS parameters and the values expected by scaling the FS parameters by $\Gamma_{\rm E}$

assumptions.value: pressure behind RS equals that at FS; same p; constant microphysical parameters

evidence.quote: make the simplifying assumption that the pressure behind the RS is equal to that at the FS
We find the peak flux density to match within 5%(!), suggesting that the RS is not magnetized relative to the FS.

used_for.value: imaging ALMA pipeline products and VLA reduction

evidence.quote: We imaged the pipeline products using the Common Astronomy Software Application
using the Python-based code EMCEE
fit them using the HEASOFT (v6.19) software package
We fit a set of galaxy templates from (cite: bc03) using `FAST`

results_numeric.quantity: ALMA light curve decline index 1.3-24.5 d

evidence.quote: The ALMA light curve can be fit with a single power law with $\alpha_1 = -0.52\pm0.02$

findings_qualitative.value: Early cm/mm excess is consistent with a Newtonian reverse shock from energy injection ending at ~0.25 d, with low ejecta magnetization

evidence.quote: The peak frequency and peak flux of the two shocks are fully self-consistent at the deceleration time, indicating low ejecta magnetization.

claims.hypothesis: Does early cm/mm and optical excess arise from a refreshed reverse shock?
claims.experiment: FS plus RS modeling of radio-to-X-ray data
claims.result: RS with g~2.8, tE~0.25 d fits the excess
claims.finding: First direct detection of energy injection RS; ejecta weakly magnetized (RB~1)

evidence.quote: the first direct detection of an energy injection RS

claims.hypothesis: What are the jet geometry and energetics?
claims.experiment: Joint modeling with ALMA, X-ray and VLA light curves constraining jet break
claims.result: t_jet~32 d, theta~13 deg, E_K~1.3e50 erg

evidence.quote: The X-ray, ALMA, and VLA observations together constrain the jet break time, $\ensuremath{t_{\rm jet}}\approx32$ d

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Relativistic RS models and other cooling-frequency orderings were ruled out

evidence.quote: Upon detailed consideration, no relativistic RS models are able to reproduce the observations

limitations_admitted.value: nu_a not constrained, causing parameter degeneracies; epsilon_e~0.9 problematic

evidence.quote: We note that $\ensuremath{\nu_{\rm a}}$ is not constrained by the data, resulting in some degeneracies between the physical parameters

referee_caveats_inferred: Radio variability from scintillation leaves cm data excluded from fits, affecting RS inference
RS analytic scalings may over-predict flux
ALMA treated as one of many datasets; RB depends on assumptions

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA data acknowledged by project code; no explicit public statement

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00819.T and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.A.00015.S.

missing_for_reproduction: Full photometry tables (only samples in text)
MCMC model code (deferred to previous papers)
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ALMA: ~tens of GB for 5 small Band 3 epochs; plus VLA and Swift
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA flux densities are tabulated but imaging details are missing and the modeling relies on external papers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The main results depend on a multi-facility model with incomplete recipe; ALMA data are a minor part.
